page: Amazon Web Services m6a.32xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor. The x86_64 platform provides 64 physical cores across 128 dedicated virtual CPUs with a 3.6 GHz clock speed, paired with 512 GB of DDR4 system memory operating at 3 GHz. This maintains a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per core. The configuration includes 50 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. It contains no onboard GPU acceleration and no bundled local storage, necessitating external network-attached volumes for persistent data storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate exceptional multi-threaded compute density and memory throughput. The system placed in the top tier for multi-core stress-ng tests at 191,273.61 and registered a PassMark CPU score of 99,308.37. It benefits from integrated hardware cryptography capabilities including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets, driving a top-tier PassMark encryption result of 151,639.74. In-memory data performance is equally robust, registering 129.17 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks alongside 9,076.97 GB/sec cached small-block read speeds and 252.01 GB/sec uncached large-block throughput.

The absence of integrated local NVMe storage and lack of AVX-512 instruction extensions represent operational tradeoffs for workloads requiring ultra-low latency scratch disks or specific vector acceleration. Nonetheless, the high core density and balanced 512 GB RAM footprint provide substantial qualitative resource value for scalable horizontal architectures. AWS m6a.32xlarge is directly aligned with large enterprise application servers, memory-intensive distributed caching layers, software compilation clusters, high-volume static web serving, and relational or document database deployments.
description: Amazon Web Services m6a.32xlarge is a general-purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor. The x86_64 platform offers 64 physical cores, 128 dedicated virtual CPUs at 3.6 GHz, and 512 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, sustaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM configuration. The instance provides 50 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, operates without bundled local storage, and includes no GPU accelerators. Benchmarks show top-tier multi-core compute throughput, scoring 99,308.37 in PassMark CPU tests and 191,273.61 in multi-core stress tests, backed by hardware-accelerated encryption instructions. Its high memory bandwidth supports exceptional key-value execution, reaching 129.17 million Redis SET operations per second. The server offers dense general-purpose capacity well suited for in-memory databases, Clang software builds, high-throughput static web hosting, and large-scale enterprise application workloads.
